title: Adam was mortal only as able to die, and immortal only as able not to die
source_text: III. Priori modo, ex eorum mente, Adam in primo statu non fuit mortalis, sed tantum posteriori. Siquidem eum mori necesse nihil erat: nec si in originali justitia perseverasset, revera fuisset mortuus. Sed tamen contingere poterat ut moreretur, quemadmodum revera post lapsum illius contigit. Per peccatum autem & ipse, & tota ejus posteritas facta est mortalis priori modo, quia necessitatem moriendi incurrit. Similiter homo in statu innocentiae priori modo non erat immortalis; nec enim erat talis qui simpliciter mori non posset. Verum immortalis erat posteriori modo, siquidem poterat non mori, & fidelis manens in Dei obsequio mortem expertus non fuisset.
pass_a_gloss: In the former way, in their mind, Adam in the first state was not mortal, but only in the latter. Since it was in no way necessary that he die: nor, if he had persevered in original justice, would he in fact have died. But yet it could happen that he died, as in fact happened after his fall. But through sin both he himself and all his posterity were made mortal in the former way, because he incurred the necessity of dying. Likewise man in the state of innocence was not immortal in the former way; for he was not such that he simply could not die. But he was immortal in the latter way, since he was able not to die, and remaining faithful in obedience to God he would not have experienced death.
pass_b_english: In their view Adam in his first state was not mortal in the first sense, only in the second. There was no necessity at all that he die, and had he persevered in original righteousness he would never actually have died. Yet it was possible for him to die, as in fact happened after his fall. Through sin he and all his descendants became mortal in the first sense, because he brought on himself the necessity of dying.

In the same way, man in the state of innocence was not immortal in the first sense, for he was not such that he simply could not die. He was immortal in the second sense: he was able not to die, and had he stayed faithful in obeying God he would never have tasted death.

lemmas.gloss: brought on himself the necessity of dying

choices.english: he was able not to die
choices.why: The Augustinian posse non mori; the English keeps the order of 'able' and 'not'.
